quotes.text: I'm disappointed with the overall performance of a full cycle of build runs. It takes a long time, and seems to be error prone. ... I like this process overall but it's just not efficient.
I also think we may have lost something by not including the shipit/forge prompts in the workflow steps.
Those should ship as the default build tools, and we also want to use them as our own.
Guards: Done needs a record, Pre-handoff checklist, Command budget
Role topics, 3 change sets; afk's content, Rhiza's words
Critic: keep, with downgrade; verifier: yes, tiered by risk; parallel leaves: later, after leaf files
Post-land CI: model-only since last green; merge rounds: yes, same rule
Extras: leaf contract, verbatim retry + run notes, model lints in review; queue journaling: yes
Plan now: the three guards, CI since last green, held-run error sources, critic downgrade; scope check: yes, fold it

fields.summary: Planned milestone 34, Efficient build cycle, from the 2026-11-12 performance report (233 run journals, 699 CI runs) and the afk prompt-gap analysis. The owner had asked for afk's shipit/forge prompts to ship as Rhiza's default build tools and accepted the orchestrator's milestone proposal. In this interview the owner picked: guards are done-needs-a-record, a builder/fixer pre-handoff checklist and a command budget (the .rhiza/log tool guard and generate-before-push are already filed as 01M76QJW and 01M76RH0; a git-safety deny was not picked); afk's prompts become one guide topic per role in three change sets (build, review, plan roles), keeping afk's content in Rhiza's words; the critic stays but can downgrade; low-risk leaves get a cheaper verifier tiered by risk; parallel leaves come later, after leaves name their files; the post-land CI round is cut by running only model checks when nothing outside .rhiza/ changed since the PR's last green commit, and the same rule covers merges of main; targets are build retries <=15% of leaves, second review cycles <=20% of runs, ship-change median <=40m and mean held time <=10m over the 30 runs after; the leaf contract, verbatim retry with run notes, deterministic model lints and queue-wait journaling are in, a lean session start is not; the scope check folds into compliance. Planned now: the three guards, CI since last green, held-run error sources and critic downgrade. Open: rhiza ci install writes only a rhiza check workflow, so where the since-last-green rule ships for other projects is parked as a question.
fields.title: Efficient build cycle milestone, with the owner
